elements.label: Figure 4.16
elements.description:
Grouped vertical bar chart. Y-axis: "Annual VND (thousand)", scale 0 to 8,000 in steps of 1,000. X-axis categories: Non-resident fee, Contributions, Parent/class fund, Uniform, Books, Other study materials, Extra courses, Other. Legend (quintile series): 1 (=poorest), 2, 3, 4, 5 (=richest), shown in progressively lighter shades of teal. No values are printed; approximate readings are:
- Non-resident fee: Q1 ~150, Q2 ~250, Q3 ~380, Q4 ~100, Q5 ~800
- Contributions: Q1 ~200, Q2 ~250, Q3 ~300, Q4 ~350, Q5 ~550
- Parent/class fund: Q1 ~120, Q2 ~180, Q3 ~230, Q4 ~330, Q5 ~500
- Uniform: Q1 ~280, Q2 ~350, Q3 ~400, Q4 ~450, Q5 ~600
- Books: Q1 ~300, Q2 ~350, Q3 ~380, Q4 ~500, Q5 ~680
- Other study materials: Q1 ~200, Q2 ~250, Q3 ~320, Q4 ~380, Q5 ~480
- Extra courses: Q1 ~1,100, Q2 ~1,700, Q3 ~2,300, Q4 ~3,300, Q5 ~6,500
- Other: Q1 ~500, Q2 ~800, Q3 ~1,650, Q4 ~2,250, Q5 ~2,700
Note printed beneath: "Other study materials include paper, pens, bags, and notebooks." Source: World Bank staff calculation using VHLSS2020. The pattern: spending rises steeply with wealth, and the gap is largest for extra courses, where the richest quintile spends several times the poorest quintile.

elements.label: Figure 4.17
elements.description:
Grouped vertical bar chart. Y-axis: "Participation rate in extra classes", scale 0 to 100 in steps of 20. X-axis: Age 8 and Age 12. Legend: Top quintile (teal), Bottom quintile (orange). Approximate values (not printed):
- Age 8: Top quintile ~77; Bottom quintile ~47
- Age 12: Top quintile ~86; Bottom quintile ~30
Source printed beneath: Le and Nguyen (2016). Young Lives Surveys. The pattern: top-quintile participation is well above bottom-quintile participation at both ages, and the gap widens with age as bottom-quintile participation falls while top-quintile participation rises.
